claims.statement: The verification loop is ordered `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit` → `pnpm lint` → `pnpm test`, cheapest signal first, and has no npm script for typecheck on purpose so typecheck reads as a step in a sequence rather than a product command; CI mirrors that order so a boundary breach or an enum the mapper forgot cannot merge.

`pnpm exec tsc --noEmit` is the only automated defence of RULES rule 18, because `DB_TO_UI_STAGE` in the batches mapper is a total map and a new DB enum variant must fail compilation until its UI treatment is chosen.

`pnpm lint` enforces RULES rules 7–10: `import/no-restricted-paths` zones in `eslint.config.mjs` put `app → modules → shared → lib/supabase` in the linter, make each module's `data/` private to other modules, forbid `shared/` importing `modules/` or `app/`, and confine `database.types.ts` to data layers.
The same ESLint block adds a warn-only `complexity: ["warn", 15]` audit, which flags maintainability cost without ever turning the lint step red.

`pnpm test` runs `vitest run` over `tests/unit/**/*.test.ts` in a `node` environment with an `@/` alias, so rule 19's guard ordering is pinned by `tests/unit/tenant-access.test.ts` asserting that `withTenantAccess` never overwrites a `sync-failed` or `unconfigured` snapshot with `no-tenant-access`.

Node 22 is hard-required and pinned in `.nvmrc` because Vitest 4's rolldown calls `util.styleText` with an array argument during startup; on Node 21 or older that throws `ERR_INVALID_ARG_VALUE` before any test file loads, so the failure surfaces as a bundler trace with no test summary.

`tests/unit/dashboard-domain.test.ts` is the shape to copy for rule 35's fixed as-of dates: it builds every case from a `dated(days)` helper with `daysToBilling` precomputed, so no clock is read anywhere in that file.

The one test that does read the clock, through the mapper's `daysUntil`, freezes it with `vi.setSystemTime` in `beforeEach` and restores with `vi.useRealTimers` in `afterEach`, asserting a day count derived from two fixed calendar dates.

`tests/unit/supabase-server.test.ts` mocks both `createClient` and Clerk's `auth`, so it proves how `lib/supabase/server.ts` decides to call them — no template argument, throwing `NO_CLERK_TOKEN_MESSAGE` on a missing token — and is explicitly not an integration test against real Supabase or Clerk.
`pnpm test:e2e` boots a real Next dev server through Playwright's `webServer: { command: 'pnpm dev' }` and runs one spec, which calls `page.goto('/dashboard')` and awaits a `/sign-in` URL.

The e2e assertion proves the gate's location: the redirect comes from `requireAuthenticatedUser()` as the first statement of the dashboard layout, not from `proxy.ts`, so a route group placed outside `(dashboard)` is what the spec catches.
A global Playwright setup project calls Clerk's `clerkSetup()` before any spec, and each spec calls `setupClerkTestingToken()` to get past bot detection.

The e2e run depends on Supabase env plus a Clerk test instance documented in `.env.example` (the `pk_test_*`/`sk_test_*` pair and `E2E_CLERK_USER_EMAIL`), so it is permission-gated, and production Clerk keys must never be used because Clerk dev and production instances issue different user IDs.

`.github/workflows/ci.yml` is a real gate — it fires on every pull request and push to `main` and runs `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit` and `pnpm test` on Node 22 with no secrets, so an import-zone breach or a non-compiling enum cannot merge; what it still does not run is `pnpm build` and `pnpm test:e2e`, because only App Router compilation catches some Server Component errors and the e2e run needs Clerk and Supabase env.

Real-Supabase RLS and tenant-isolation tests are outstanding: `docs/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md` reserves `tests/integration/` and `tests/security/` but neither directory exists, so every authorization claim rests on reading migrations.

Because RLS tests must hit the hosted project with no mocks, they are gated by RULES rule 36's permission requirement, and a missing Supabase env makes them fail in a way that reads like a policy bug.

The suite leaves the I/O half of `data/` functions uncovered in places — the write flow of `importLearnersCsv` has no test while its `domain/` half and pure `summariseWrites` do — so thin-looking files must be read for whether the missing coverage is I/O before being taken as regression.

RULES.md §9 is stale in the repo: rule 34 still says there is no test runner and that `pnpm test` is a placeholder, while `package.json` defines it as `vitest run` and rules 7–10 are already lint-enforced.

`pnpm lint` is the bare `eslint` script over the flat config, so the strict zone set of `import/no-restricted-paths` is what the linter applies; it must be run locally before every push because it is the only automated enforcement of those import rules and the local run is where an agent or author sees the violation.

CI's `ci.yml` is the repository's only merge-blocking gate: it runs a single `check` job on Node 22 (checkout, pnpm setup, setup-node, `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, then `pnpm lint` → `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit` → `pnpm test`), cancels superseded runs via a `concurrency` group on `github.ref`, holds a 15-minute timeout with `contents: read`, and needs no secrets because the unit suite makes no Supabase or Clerk call.

The other workflows do not gate code: `openwiki-update.yml` commits regenerated wiki pages, `claude.yml`/`claude-code-review.yml` post agent commentary, `stale.yml` closes idle issues, and `qodana.yml` runs the `qodana-js` starter profile whose `failureConditions` block is left commented out in `qodana.yaml`, so it reports findings without a severity threshold that can fail a run.

A green check says nothing about RLS: `tests/integration/` and `tests/security/` — the directories `docs/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md` §5.3 reserves for real-Supabase isolation and security tests — do not exist, so green covers domain and mapper correctness only and a tenant leak ships green; the nearest thing, `tests/unit/tenant-scope.test.ts`, is a pure test of the JS selection layer.

Each of the three loop steps defends a distinct rule level and ordering is cheapest-signal first: `tsc --noEmit` is the `[types]` force behind the total `DB_TO_UI_STAGE` bridge, `pnpm lint` is the `[lint]` force behind the `import/no-restricted-paths` layer zones, and `pnpm test` is the only place `[review]`-tagged behaviour such as rule 19's guard ordering gets a pinned check.

`vi.setSystemTime` is called exactly once in the entire suite — in `batches.test.ts`'s days-to-billing block, hooked in `beforeEach` with `vi.useRealTimers()` in `afterEach` — because the production mapper is the only place a real clock is read; the rest of the suite takes its as-of date as input, which is the preferred shape.

`E2E_CLERK_USER_EMAIL` and `E2E_CLERK_USER_PASSWORD` are declared in `.env.example` alongside a `pk_test_*`/`sk_test_*` pair with the instruction to use test keys only, while the single spec `e2e/auth.spec.ts` needs only the anonymous `/dashboard` → `/sign-in` redirect, so the signed-in e2e cases those variables serve are still unwritten.
